meta.description: Presents and manages the administrative navigation menu for authorised admin users in the CardDemo credit card management system.
meta.process_description: When an admin user successfully logs in, this program displays a role-specific menu screen listing up to 10 administrative functions available within the CardDemo system. The user selects a numbered option, and the program validates the selection before transferring control to the corresponding administrative sub-program. If the selected option corresponds to a function that has not yet been installed or activated (marked as 'DUMMY'), the program informs the user that the option is unavailable rather than attempting to launch it. If no valid session context exists (communication area is empty), the user is redirected back to the sign-on screen, enforcing session integrity.

files.USRSEC: User security file used to validate and retrieve user credentials and role information for access control

business_rules: Only authenticated admin users with a valid session (non-empty communication area) may access the admin menu; unauthenticated or session-less users are immediately redirected to the sign-on screen.

A user-entered menu option must be numeric, non-zero, and must not exceed the total number of configured administrative options; any invalid entry results in an error message and the menu is re-displayed.
Administrative menu options flagged as 'DUMMY' are recognised as not yet installed; the system informs the user the option is unavailable and does not attempt to launch the corresponding program.
Pressing PF3 at any point returns the user to the sign-on screen, providing a controlled and secure exit from the admin menu.
The menu supports a maximum of 10 displayable administrative options; any options beyond 10 configured in the system are silently ignored in the display.
Control is transferred to sub-programs via CICS XCTL, passing the shared communication area to maintain session context and navigation history across the admin workflow.
Any key press other than Enter or PF3 is treated as invalid and results in an 'invalid key' error message, preventing unintended navigation actions.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Top-level working storage group that holds all operational variables used by the admin menu program during a user's session, including navigation state, error handling, and user input processing.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The name of the current admin menu program (COADM01C). This is passed through the communication area so that sub-programs and the CICS runtime know which screen the admin user came from, enabling correct back-navigation and audit trail tracking across the admin workflow.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier (CA00) for the admin menu. When a sub-program finishes its task and needs to return control to the admin menu, this transaction ID is used to re-invoke the correct menu screen, maintaining the continuity of the admin user's session.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The feedback message displayed to the admin user on the menu screen. This communicates the outcome of their last action — for example, notifying them that they entered an invalid menu option, that a selected function is not yet available, or that they pressed an unrecognised key.

variables.name: WS-USRSEC-FILE
variables.description: The logical file name of the User Security file (USRSEC). This file is used to validate that the person accessing the admin menu is an authenticated user with the appropriate administrative role, enforcing access control before the menu is displayed.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator that tracks whether the admin user's menu option selection has failed validation. When set to 'Y', it signals that the menu must be re-displayed with an appropriate error message rather than proceeding to launch an administrative function.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: A named condition that is true when a validation error has occurred during menu option selection (e.g., non-numeric input, out-of-range option, or unavailable function). Used in business logic to trigger re-display of the menu with an error message.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: A named condition that is true when no validation error has occurred, meaning the admin user's menu selection is valid and the system can proceed to transfer control to the selected administrative function.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after executing a CICS command (such as reading the user security file or transferring control to a sub-program). Used to detect whether a system-level operation succeeded or failed, enabling appropriate error handling to protect the integrity of the admin session.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code that accompanies the response code, providing additional detail about why a CICS operation failed. Together with WS-RESP-CD, this helps diagnose specific failure conditions such as a missing security record or an unavailable program during admin navigation.

variables.name: WS-OPTION-X
variables.description: A working field that holds the raw menu option entered by the admin user as alphanumeric text, right-justified. It is used as an intermediate step to clean and validate the user's input (e.g., stripping spaces) before converting it into a numeric value for range checking and program selection.

variables.name: WS-OPTION
variables.description: The validated numeric menu option chosen by the admin user. This numeric value is used to look up the corresponding administrative function (e.g., User List, Account Management) in the menu options table and determine which sub-program to launch via CICS transfer of control.

variables.name: WS-IDX
variables.description: A loop counter used when iterating through the list of configured administrative menu options — for example, when building the on-screen display of available options or when trimming trailing spaces from user input. It ensures each option is processed in sequence up to the configured maximum.

variables.name: WS-ADMIN-OPT-TXT
variables.description: A working field that temporarily holds the display name of an administrative menu option (e.g., 'User List (Security)') while it is being prepared for rendering on the admin menu screen. It acts as a staging area to format and present each option's label to the admin user.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area passed between programs during the admin session. Its presence (non-empty) confirms that the user has an active, authenticated session. It carries session context — including user identity, role, and navigation history — across all programs in the CardDemo admin workflow.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: The linkage section representation of the CICS communication area, defined minimally as a single byte. Its primary business purpose is to detect whether a communication area was passed to this program at all — if it is empty or absent, the user has no valid session and must be redirected to the sign-on screen for authentication.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration entry point of the admin menu program. It enforces session integrity, controls first-time versus returning screen display, routes user key presses to the appropriate business action, and ensures the CICS session is kept alive for continued admin navigation.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph processes the admin user's menu selection when they press Enter, validating the chosen option number and either launching the corresponding administrative function or informing the user that the selected option is not yet available.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-SIGNON-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the secure exit from the admin menu by redirecting the user back to the bank's sign-on screen, ensuring no admin session remains open without proper re-authentication. It acts as the controlled logout pathway, enforcing session integrity by always landing the user at a known, safe entry point.

paragraphs.name: SEND-MENU-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph assembles and renders the administrative navigation menu screen for the authenticated admin user. It combines header information, the list of available administrative functions, and any status or error messages before presenting the fully built screen to the user.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-MENU-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: Captures the admin user's menu selection submitted from the administrative navigation screen. This step collects whatever option the user has entered before the system proceeds to validate and act on their choice.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: Prepares the standard header information displayed at the top of the administrative menu screen, including application titles, the current date and time, and identifiers that allow the user and support staff to identify which screen and transaction they are working in.

paragraphs.name: BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS
paragraphs.description: Constructs and populates the administrative menu screen by formatting each configured administrative function as a numbered display entry. This ensures the admin user sees a clean, sequentially numbered list of available system functions, limited to a maximum of 10 visible options.

paragraphs.name: PGMIDERR-ERR-PARA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the scenario where an admin user selects a menu option that has not yet been installed or activated in the system. It informs the user that the chosen function is unavailable and returns them to the admin menu, maintaining their active session.
